$description: Golden vectors for the positional wire format's primitives — TYPES_INTERFACE.md → Serialization → Primitives. Every entry is asserted both directions unless it sets "decode": false.

vectors.name: u8/max
vectors.note: A bare u8 spans the whole byte, which is why its writer throws rather than sentinelling: 0xff is a legal value, so it could not also mean 'malformed'. The u8 FIELDS in the layout tables are booleans and enum8 tags, whose domains are narrower and which stay total.

vectors.name: vlqU/max-safe-integer
vectors.note: 2^53-1, the top of the `number` encodable domain. Eight bytes — which is why the ten-byte sentinel is unreachable from a valid field.

vectors.name: vlqU/sentinel-nan
vectors.note: The all-ones u64 sentinel — unreachable from a valid `number` field, so a malformed value never collides with a well-formed one (TYPES_INTERFACE -> Totality).

vectors.name: vlqU/sentinel-past-safe-integer
vectors.note: 2^53 — one past the domain. The first value the sentinel has to catch rather than encode.

vectors.name: vlqU/sentinel-wrong-type
vectors.note: A numeric string must not coerce — "7" and 7 would otherwise share an encoding.

vectors.name: vlqS/minus-one
vectors.note: The transfer sentinel `heightOrTransfer` carried by credit.proofSource — the reason that field is vlqS and not vlqU.

vectors.name: vlqS/max-encodable
vectors.note: 2^52-1. ZigZag doubles before the VLQ sees it, so the signed domain is half the unsigned one.

vectors.name: vlqS/min-encodable
vectors.note: -2^52, whose zigzag is exactly 2^53-1 — the widest signed encoding, still eight bytes.

vectors.name: vlqS/sentinel-past-domain
vectors.note: 2^52 zigzags to 2^53, one past safe — so it sentinels rather than throwing.

vectors.name: vlqU64/max-safe-integer
vectors.note: Byte-identical to vlqU/max-safe-integer. The two paths are two views of one encoding — WIRE_INTERFACE → BigInt VLQ.

vectors.name: vlqU64/first-past-safe-integer
vectors.note: 2^53 — the first value only the bigint path can carry.

vectors.name: vlqU64/u64-max
vectors.note: ⚠ These are the sentinel's bytes, and here they are a LEGAL value. That is precisely why the bigint writer throws instead of sentinelling — TYPES_INTERFACE -> Totality.

vectors.name: b32hex/byte-ordered
vectors.note: The whole point of b32: an id's in-memory hex becomes 32 RAW bytes — no length prefix, and no second hexing.

vectors.name: b32hex/all-ones
vectors.note: In-domain, which is why a fixed-width field has no unreachable sentinel and its writer throws.

vectors.name: b33hex/empty-state-root
vectors.note: EMPTY_STATE_ROOT. The AVL+ digest is 33 bytes, not 32 — the single easiest field in the header to get wrong.

vectors.name: b32bytes/byte-ordered
vectors.note: Post.author and Post.challenge are Uint8Array in memory, not hex — same 32 wire bytes, different in-memory type.

vectors.name: b64bytes/byte-ordered
vectors.note: A 64-byte Ed25519 signature.

vectors.name: lp/single-zero-byte
vectors.note: Distinct from lp/empty: the length prefix is what keeps a zero byte from vanishing.

vectors.name: lp/sentinel-wrong-type
vectors.note: A length-prefixed field sentinels its LENGTH — a real byte length is a safe integer, so the all-ones u64 is unreachable there too.

vectors.name: lpUtf8/two-byte-sequence
vectors.note: U+00E9. The prefix counts BYTES, not code points — 1 character, 2 bytes.

vectors.name: lpUtf8/four-byte-sequence
vectors.note: U+1F600 — outside the BMP, so it is 2 UTF-16 units and 4 UTF-8 bytes. An implementation counting `.length` in JS would write 2 here.

vectors.name: lpUtf8/mixed-widths
vectors.note: 18 bytes from 10 code points across all four UTF-8 widths.

vectors.name: lpUtf8/sentinel-wrong-type
vectors.note: TextEncoder coerces through String(), so without the type check `undefined` and "undefined" would share bytes.

vectors.name: arr/empty
vectors.note: An empty array is a one-byte count, not zero bytes — which is what makes it distinguishable from an omitted field.

vectors.name: arr/two-elements
vectors.note: The count is what makes concatenated variable-length elements injective — the defect audit M-1 closed.

vectors.name: arr/of-vlqU
vectors.note: Count 3, then three variable-width elements — 1, 1 and 2 bytes.

vectors.name: arr/nested-empty-strings
vectors.note: Two empty elements are not the same bytes as an empty array — count 2, then two zero-length prefixes.

vectors.name: opt/present-zero
vectors.note: ⚠ The pair that matters: absent is `00`, present-with-a-zero-value is `01 00`. A format that conflated them would let a field be dropped without changing the hash.

vectors.name: opt/present-empty-string
vectors.note: Present-but-empty again, this time where the value itself encodes to zero payload bytes.

vectors.name: opt/present-false
vectors.note: decayBurn?: boolean — `false` present must differ from absent, or a box loses a committed field silently.

vectors.name: enum8/sentinel-unknown-value
vectors.note: The tag set is narrower than the byte, so 0xff is a reachable sentinel here — and enum8() refuses to build a table that claims it.
